polaris: A: Srivastava-style orbital-overlap integral absorbs the main structural explanatory power for transport/effective mass; B: graph spectral features retain independent predictive power after controlling overlap, onsite variance, density, mobility-edge margin, batch and finite-size.
framework: Amorphous oxide semiconductor electronic-structure baseline: metal-s orbital overlap integral -> effective-mass/transport proxy, followed by same-sample residual tests for graph spectra.
findings: Round 1 supports a strict baseline-first protocol. Srivastava et al. 2019 already argue that electron transport in multicomponent amorphous ionic semiconductors can be explained by an orbital-overlap integral computed from structural information and directly correlated with carrier effective mass. Therefore LP29 graph metrics that are monotone summaries of pair overlap, cation distance, coordination, or weighted degree should be treated as reparameterizations unless they predict external residual labels after the overlap baseline and controls. The plausible non-absorbed metrics are normalized/bottleneck spectral quantities and perturbation responses, especially lambda_2 at fixed overlap distribution, spectral radius after degree/weight-preserving controls, and high-betweenness targeted damage relative to matched random damage.
weakest_link: The exact Srivastava overlap normalization must be extracted from the full article/SI before numerical reproduction; MCP metadata and abstract establish the baseline claim but not every implementation constant. C2 is therefore a protocol-level result, not yet a numerical defeat or survival of graph metrics.
next_plan: Fill the same-sample table for Srivastava a-IGZO/a-ZnON, Jankousky a-In2O3 structures/SI, and Furubayashi a-ITO transport where possible; then fit external residual labels against overlap baseline plus controls before testing graph spectral residual features.
literature_needed: Srivastava 2019 orbital overlap integral full text/SI; Jankousky 2026 a-In2O3 structures and spectral-function data; Furubayashi 2019 Hall mobility/thickness/density tables; Jang 2025 amorphous-to-crystalline In2O3/IGZO mobility-trend SI.

minimal_math.pair_set: E_s(r_c) = cation-cation pairs within cutoff r_c, usually metal-s conduction centers
minimal_math.baseline_effective_mass: log(m_eff_s/m0) = beta_0 + beta_1*log(1/(O_s + eps)) + beta_2*V_s + beta_3*x_density_s + beta_batch[b_s]
minimal_math.baseline_transport: log(mu_s) = gamma_0 + gamma_1*log(O_s + eps) + gamma_2*log(n_s) + gamma_3*DeltaE_s + gamma_4*V_s + gamma_batch[b_s]
minimal_math.residual_label: r_y_s = y_s - f_y(O_s, V_s, n_s, DeltaE_s, batch_s, size_s)
minimal_math.graph_residual_test: r_y_s = alpha_0 + alpha_1*lambda2_resid_s + alpha_2*rho_resid_s + alpha_3*damage_resid_s + error_s

units_and_variables.rho_ij: same length unit as d_ij; orbital decay length or fitted species-pair decay parameter

inspector_check.formula: O_s = Sum(q_i*q_j*exp(-d_ij/rho_ij), (i,j) in E_s)/N_pair_s; residual labels r_y_s are defined after f_y(O_s,V_s,n_s,DeltaE_s,batch_s,size_s).
inspector_check.direction: Graph metrics are admissible only as residual predictors after the overlap baseline, not as primary structural explanations.
assumptions: Metal-s dominated conduction centers define the pair graph.
The exponential pair-overlap proxy is acceptable until the exact Srivastava normalization is extracted.
External labels are same-sample or explicitly provenance-joined, not family-level averages.

join_rules: Use exact same sample_id when structure and transport are from the same film or calculation ensemble member.
Use family_join_flag=true only for literature-level comparison; family joins cannot support the decisive C2 residual claim.
Batch and finite-size controls are mandatory columns, not post-hoc notes.
Graph features must be recomputed on the same edge set used for overlap or on a declared alternative edge set with an overlap-preserving null model.

absorbed_by_overlap_baseline.reason: It is approximately Sum(W_ij)/N and therefore a direct rewriting of normalized orbital overlap.

absorbed_by_overlap_baseline.metric: mean cation-cation distance or short-bond fraction
absorbed_by_overlap_baseline.reason: For monotone overlap kernels S_ij=exp(-d_ij/rho_ij), distance summaries are low-order proxies for O_s.
If edges are thresholded by overlap/distance, coordination is the binary coarse-graining of the overlap integral.
Without threshold sweeps and overlap-preserving nulls, giant component mainly reports whether enough pair overlaps are above cutoff.

absorbed_by_overlap_baseline.metric: O-O defect fraction when it only shifts carrier density or onsite variance
absorbed_by_overlap_baseline.reason: It must enter as density/onsite/mobility-edge control unless it creates a distinct graph bottleneck effect.

not_absorbed_if_controls_pass.condition: Computed after fixing total overlap, weighted-degree sequence, density and size; detects global bottleneck/connectivity not reducible to pair-sum overlap.
Only admissible after degree/weight-preserving rewiring; otherwise it is partly a weighted-degree proxy.
Admissible as a perturbation-response observable if targeted edge weakening causes larger residual transport/spectral loss than matched random weakening at fixed overlap removed.
Can survive if two structures share O_s and V_s but differ in inter-community necks that control extended-state percolation.

not_absorbed_if_controls_pass.metric: finite-size scaling exponent of spectral gap
not_absorbed_if_controls_pass.condition: Potentially independent if it tracks delocalization transition scaling rather than local pair strength.

deepening_1_consequence_layers: If overlap absorbs graph metrics, LP29 reduces from a graph-spectral mechanism to a known structure-to-effective-mass descriptor, and the graph vocabulary is only a visualization layer.

Second-layer consequence: the decisive experiment becomes accurate overlap/onsite/density measurement, not graph perturbation; new claims must move to better overlap descriptors or measurement protocol.
deepening_2_weakest_assumption_layers: The most fragile premise is that a scalar normalized overlap O_s is sufficient for transport/effective mass across amorphous structures.

Second-layer risk: even if O_s predicts m_eff, transport may depend on spatial arrangement of strong overlaps, so a scalar effective-mass baseline can be true while bottleneck graph residuals still matter.
deepening.hard_boundary: No numerical survival claim for graph residuals can be made until exact Srivastava normalization and same-sample rows are filled.

claims.statement: LP29 graph metrics that are monotone functions of pair overlap, distance thresholding, or weighted degree should be treated as absorbed by the orbital-overlap baseline.
